title: Closing an inflationary gap

readouts.v: In this model the price level falls; in practice a rate rise usually slows inflation.

predict.q: Output is 520, but full-employment output is 500. What should the central bank do to close the gap?

options.s: Cut the rate: cheaper borrowing raises output, which brings prices down
options.fb: A rate cut shifts AD right, so output and prices rise further above full employment.

options.s: Raise the rate: AD shifts left, so output falls back to 500 and the price level is lower
options.fb: A rise of 2 points shifts AD left until output is 500: the gap closes, with the price level at 100.

options.s: Raise the rate: LRAS shifts right to 520, so the gap disappears
options.fb: Interest rates act on AD. LRAS (productive capacity) does not move to 520.

options.s: Raise the rate: AD shifts left, but output stays at 520 and only the price level falls
options.fb: SRAS slopes upward, so in the short run lower AD lowers output as well as the price level.

task: Move the policy rate slider and watch AD, real output, the price level and the gap.

target.do: Raise the policy rate, then press Check.

takeaway: A rate rise shifts AD left. Too small leaves a gap; too large pushes output below full employment.
